candidate_profile.description: The candidate reaches the right broad answer: keep the chilled juice business and improve it. They identify the main economic drivers, but their prioritization and synthesis are solid rather than outstanding.
behaviour_rules: Start with a concise recap and ask a couple of relevant questions about market structure, profitability, and cost drivers.
Use a workable framework covering competition, cost structure, pricing, and strategic fit.
Recognize that the large players benefit from greater scale and can spend more on advertising, promotions, trade, and coupons.
Correctly identify that the client's more elaborate blend likely carries a cost disadvantage because some flavorings are significantly more expensive.
Explain that the market is price sensitive, so the client cannot easily recover the cost difference through premium pricing.
Acknowledge brand and manufacturing synergies across the three juice formats.
Recommend keeping the chilled juice business and reworking ingredient mix and costs, though the recommendation may still be somewhat concise.

expected_issues: Reasoning is mostly correct but may not be tightly prioritized.
May mention synergies and cost issues without fully synthesizing why selling is inferior.
Recommendation is sound, but not especially sharp on implementation detail.
expected_feedback_points: Good diagnosis of the scale, promotion, and cost-structure disadvantage.
Good recognition that price-sensitive consumers limit the client's pricing power.
Correct acknowledgment of brand and plant synergies.
Correct recommendation to keep the business and improve ingredients and costs.
To improve further, sharpen prioritization and deliver a more executive-level final synthesis.
